edges.description: Cleft palate is associated with the recurrent p.Arg2686His variant. The developmental route from PIEZO2 gain of function to failed palatal closure is not described in the cited sources.
Ptosis is reported across the dominant PIEZO2 spectrum; the mechanism linking PIEZO2 gain of function to eyelid and extraocular involvement is not established.
Posterior fossa malformation in PIEZO2-positive patients suggests a role for PIEZO2 in hindbrain development; the mechanism is unknown and the association rests on few cases.
The signal released from overactive sensory endings that alters tendon and joint development has not been identified.

nodes.description: PIEZO2 is the principal mechanotransduction channel of proprioceptive sensory neurons, which innervate muscle spindles and tendon organs. In mice, expressing a gain-of-function Piezo2 allele only in these neurons is sufficient to reproduce the limb contractures, whereas expressing it only in limb mesenchyme (muscle, cartilage and tendon) is not. The effect depends on neuronal activity during a postnatal developmental window, and botulinum toxin, but not motor-endplate blockade with alpha-bungarotoxin, prevents it. The authors interpret this as an efferent action of the afferent nerve endings, likely through increased exocytosis, rather than increased reflex motor drive; stretch-evoked muscle spindle afferent firing was not increased ex vivo. The node is PROVISIONAL because the evidence is from a mouse carrying a distal arthrogryposis type 5 allele, not the Gordon syndrome variant.

nodes.description: Mouse carrying the mouse equivalent of the human distal arthrogryposis type 5 variant E2727del, expressed constitutively or restricted by Cre driver to proprioceptive neurons (Pvalb), all sensory neurons (Advillin, inducible) or limb mesenchyme (Prrx1). Constitutive and proprioceptor-restricted mice develop hindlimb contractures and shortened tendons; mesenchyme-restricted mice do not. Botulinum toxin injected into the hindlimb at postnatal days 7 to 10, or a maternal diet enriched in eicosapentaenoic acid, which shortens PIEZO2 inactivation, reduced the defects.

Failure of the secondary palate to close completely, giving cleft palate or its minor form, bifid uvula. nodes.description: Heterozygous dominant PIEZO2 variants alter the kinetics of the mechanically activated channel rather than abolishing it. The dominant variants characterized by patch clamp (E2727del and I802F, from distal arthrogryposis type 5 families) make PIEZO2-dependent currents recover faster from inactivation, and E2727del also slows inactivation, so the channel passes more current for a given mechanical stimulus. Mutant channels are not constitutively open and are not toxic to cells. The recurrent Gordon syndrome variant p.Arg2686His is treated as acting the same way by inference from these alleles. The node name is shared with the Marden-Walker syndrome entry because the lesion is the same.
